The Two Classes

The seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent

Thesis. From the gate of Eden God Himself divided mankind into two classes, and only two: "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed" (Gen. 3:15). The enmity is God-put; the classes are not races or ranks but worshipers — Abel, who brought the appointed lamb by faith, and Cain, who brought the fruit of his own hands and his own way. From that altar the two lines diverge and never merge: Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and builded a city; Seth's line began to call upon the name of the LORD, dwelt apart, and walked with God. The serpent's seed congregates — cities, plains, valleys, convenience, the arts of a civilization that forgets God — and attacks the institutions of Eden: marriage by polygamy, appetite by indulgence, and appointed worship by will-worship. The woman's seed are pilgrims and strangers — tents, altars, mountains, the wilderness — a peculiar people who worship in spirit and in truth, needing no city. And every time God's people have mingled with the world — the sons of God taking the daughters of men, Israel joined to Baal-peor and demanding a king "like all the nations," the church seeking the favor of the empire — the peculiar people lost their peculiarity, and the distinction had to be remade by judgment: the flood, the scattering, the wilderness. Christ fixed the type for the last age: "as it was in the days of Noah... as it was in the days of Lot." The two classes stand at last fully formed and fully visible — they that worship the beast and his image, and they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus — and the final call of the everlasting gospel is the old call of the ark and of Sodom's gate: "Come out of her, my people."

Method. After Haskell's Bible Handbook: ref → gloss, scannable; every symbol and doctrine defined FIRST from Scripture (Miller's Rule — the Bible defines its own figures). The argument is built from the text — Genesis 3-6 (the two seeds, the two offerings, the two lineages, the mingling), Genesis 11-19 (Babel, Abraham the pilgrim, Lot in the plain), Numbers 22-25 and 1 Samuel 8 (Israel mingling), Hebrews 11 (the cloud of witnesses, pilgrims and strangers), Luke 17 and Matthew 24 (the days of Noah and of Lot), and Revelation 7, 12-14, 18 (the seal, the mark, the woman in the wilderness, the final call). Ellen White and the pioneers are the SECONDARY but indispensable witnesses — Patriarchs and Prophets 81-82 names 'the two classes' outright (Sethites in the mountains, Cainites in the plains), and Great Controversy supplies the church-world union and the Waldenses in the mountains. Quote every refcode verbatim; verify with bible egw "REF"; never invent one, and never let a doctrine or symbol rest on the testimony where Scripture must carry it.

Part I — The Two Seeds

¶1. The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall

At the gate of Eden God HIMSELF declares war — "I will put enmity" — and by one sentence divides mankind into exactly two seeds, the woman's and the serpent's. The enmity is grace, not curse: fallen man is naturally at peace with Satan, and the whole controversy from Abel's altar to the remnant is the history of that God-put antagonism — and of what happens when it is lost.

The charter — God puts the enmity — Gen. 3:14-15:

  • Gen. 3:14. "And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field" — the verdict falls on the serpent first; the curse is his. What follows in v. 15 is spoken TO the serpent but given FOR the man: not more curse, but the first promise.
  • Gen. 3:15. "And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel" — the charter of the whole study. Mark the "I": God is the author of the enmity, not fallen man; and by one sentence He divides the race into exactly two seeds — the woman's and the serpent's — locked in a war that ends with a bruised heel and a crushed head.
    • the enmity = the God-PUT antagonism between the two seeds — grace, not curse. "I will put enmity" (Gen. 3:15): it is not native to fallen man, whose evil nature is at peace with the originator of sin; friendship with the world IS enmity with God (Jas. 4:4), and the world's hatred of the saints is this same enmity running outward, because Christ chose them out of the world (John 15:19). Defined in full at the close.
  • GC 505.2. White: "God declares: 'I will put enmity.' This enmity is not naturally entertained. When man transgressed the divine law, his nature became evil, and he was in harmony, and not at variance, with Satan... Had not God specially interposed, Satan and man would have entered into an alliance against Heaven; and instead of cherishing enmity against Satan, the whole human family would have been united in opposition to God" — the exact grace-thesis, opening with the very words of Gen. 3:15: the fallen natural state is PEACE with the serpent; the enmity is God's special interposition, and without it the race is one seed only — Satan's.
  • GC 506.2. White: "It is the grace that Christ implants in the soul which creates in man enmity against Satan. Without this converting grace and renewing power, man would continue the captive of Satan... But the new principle in the soul creates conflict where hitherto had been peace" — the enmity named outright as implanted grace: "conflict where hitherto had been peace." The antagonism is a gift, and the gift is Christ's; to feel no war with Satan is the mark of still belonging to him.

The seed of the woman — Christ first, and His people in Him — Gal. 3:16, 29; Rom. 16:20; Matt. 13:37:

  • Gal. 3:16. "He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ" — Scripture defines its own figure: the promised Seed is SINGULAR, and it is Christ. The seed of the woman is Christ first, before it is anyone else.
    • the seed of the woman = Christ first, and in Him His people. The singular "seed" is Christ (Gal. 3:16); those who are Christ's are then reckoned that same seed (Gal. 3:29); the Seed's head-bruising is shared with the church (Rom. 16:20); Christ Himself sows the class as "the good seed... the children of the kingdom" (Matt. 13:37-38); and the line runs to "the remnant of her seed" at the end (Rev. 12:17). Defined in full at the close.
  • Gal. 3:29. "And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise" — in Him, His people become the seed. The class is defined by belonging to Christ, not by bloodline; membership is by union, not descent.
  • Rom. 16:20. "And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" — Gen. 3:15's head-bruising applied to the church: "under YOUR feet." The woman's seed includes the saints in Christ, who share the Seed's victory over the serpent.
  • Matt. 13:37. "He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man" — the woman's seed is planted by the Son of man Himself; Christ both IS the Seed and SOWS the seed-class.

The seed of the serpent — paternity by practice, not blood — John 8:44; Matt. 13:38-39; 1 John 3:12:

  • John 8:44. "Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning... When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it" — Christ defines the serpent's seed as SPIRITUAL paternity: religious men, sons of Abraham after the flesh, are "of your father the devil" because they DO his lusts. Fatherhood here is moral, not biological.
    • the seed of the serpent = not a bloodline but a spiritual paternity — those who belong to the devil by doing his works: "ye are of your father the devil" for "the lusts of your father ye will do" (John 8:44); the tares are "the children of the wicked one," sown by the devil (Matt. 13:38-39); Cain, a natural son of Eve, is "of that wicked one" (1 John 3:12); the standing test is practice (1 John 3:8, 10). Defined in full at the close.
  • Matt. 13:38-39. "The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world" — the two seeds are the two paternities: children of the kingdom and children of the wicked one, and no third planting. The classes grow together in one field until the harvest at the end of the world.
  • 1 John 3:12. "Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous" — the proof-case: Cain, a physical son of Adam and Eve, is "of that wicked one." The first murderer belonged to the devil while sharing Abel's parents — the serpent's seed is by spirit, never by descent; and the murder itself is the enmity of the serpent's seed against the woman's.
  • COL 152.1. White: "The Pharisee and the publican represent two great classes into which those who come to worship God are divided. Their first two representatives are found in the first two children that were born into the world" — the two classes traced to Cain and Abel at the altar: Cain "came to God with a thank offering only," but Abel "came with the blood that pointed to the Lamb of God" — the original heads of the serpent's line and the woman's.
  • PP 72.5. White: "Cain and Abel represent two classes that will exist in the world till the close of time. One class avail themselves of the appointed sacrifice for sin; the other venture to depend upon their own merits" — exactly two classes, lasting "till the close of time," and the dividing question is the appointed sacrifice — the blood received or refused.
  • PP 74.2. White: "Cain hated and killed his brother, not for any wrong that Abel had done, but 'because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.' 1 John 3:12. So in all ages the wicked have hated those who were better than themselves" — Ellen White cites John's verdict herself and generalizes it to "all ages": the serpent's seed hating the woman's is the standing pattern of history.

The test of the two classes — doing, not descent — 1 John 3:8-10:

  • 1 John 3:8. "He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil" — the defining criterion of the serpent's seed: practice. And in the same breath the head-bruising of Gen. 3:15 restated: the Son of God manifested "that he might destroy the works of the devil" is the Seed come to crush the head.
  • 1 John 3:9. "Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God" — the mirror truth for the woman's line: the divine seed "remaineth in him." The righteous class also stands by paternity — born of God, the seed abiding within — not by pedigree.
  • 1 John 3:10. "In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother" — the two classes named explicitly — "children of God" and "children of the devil" — and told apart by doing righteousness and loving the brethren. Scripture knows no third class.

No neutral ground — to lose the enmity is to change sides — Jas. 4:4; John 15:19:

  • Jas. 4:4. "know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God" — there is no neutral ground. The enmity points one way or the other: to lose the God-put enmity toward the serpent's world is not to become neutral but to relocate the enmity — against God.
  • John 15:19. "If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you" — Christ traces the enmity forward: the world hates His people BECAUSE He has chosen them out of it. The hatred the woman's seed endures is the same God-put antagonism running outward — the hatred is the evidence of the grace.
  • SR 62.1. White: "The descendants of Seth were called the sons of God; the descendants of Cain, the sons of men. As the sons of God mingled with the sons of men, they became corrupt and, by intermarriage with them, lost... their peculiar, holy character" — the historical anchor of the danger: MINGLING the two classes cost the woman's line its distinction. (The "sons of God" of Gen. 6:2 are here read as the covenant line of Seth, not angels: Adam was "the son of God" (Luke 3:38), and the covenant people are "the children of the LORD your God" (Deut. 14:1) — sonship by covenant standing, the reading the two-class frame requires; the mingling is traced in full in "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity.")
  • PP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate... But in the lapse of time they ventured, little by little, to mingle with the inhabitants of the valleys. This association was productive of the worst results... they lost their peculiar, holy character" — the arc in detail: the Sethites withdrew to the mountains and were preserved; they mingled with the Cainite valleys "little by little" and were ruined. Separation preserved the enmity; incremental mingling dissolved it — the recurring ruin the enmity was put to prevent.

The terminus — the dragon and the remnant of her seed — Rev. 12:9, 17:

  • Rev. 12:9. "And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world" — Scripture's own identification, closing the chain: the dragon of Revelation 12 IS "that old serpent" of Eden. The war of Gen. 3:15 and the war of Rev. 12:17 are one war, with one enemy.
  • Rev. 12:17. "And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ" — the end-time terminus of Gen. 3:15: the dragon (that old serpent — Rev. 12:9) wars on "the remnant of her seed" — the LAST of the woman's line, marked by commandment-keeping and the testimony of Jesus. The two-seed war opened at Eden runs unbroken to the close.
  • MWV2 213.1. Miller: "it is evident by the expression 'remnant of her seed,' that it means the last of the church 'who keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ'" — the pioneer definition: the remnant of her seed = the commandment-keeping last of the church, the final generation of the woman's line under the serpent's final wrath.

DEFINITION — THE ENMITY — TWO SEEDS FROM ONE FALL = at the fall God Himself interposed an antagonism — "I will put enmity" (Gen. 3:15) — dividing mankind into exactly two seeds and only two. The seed of the woman is Christ first, the singular Seed of promise (Gal. 3:16), and in Him all who are His (Gal. 3:29), sown by the Son of man as "the children of the kingdom" (Matt. 13:37-38), sharing His bruising of the serpent's head — "under YOUR feet" (Rom. 16:20) — down to "the remnant of her seed" at the end (Rev. 12:17). The seed of the serpent is no bloodline but a paternity of practice: "ye are of your father the devil" because "the lusts of your father ye will do" (John 8:44); the tares are "the children of the wicked one," sown by the devil (Matt. 13:38-39); Cain, Eve's own son, was "of that wicked one" (1 John 3:12); "he that committeth sin is of the devil" (1 John 3:8), while the born of God carry the divine seed remaining in them (1 John 3:9) — "the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil" (1 John 3:10), and Scripture admits no third class. The enmity between them is GRACE, not curse: fallen man's nature was "in harmony, and not at variance, with Satan," and without God's special interposition "the whole human family would have been united in opposition to God" (GC 505.2); it is "the grace that Christ implants in the soul" that "creates conflict where hitherto had been peace" (GC 506.2). Therefore no neutral ground exists — "the friendship of the world is enmity with God" (Jas. 4:4) — and the world's hatred of the saints is the same enmity running outward, for Christ has "chosen you out of the world" (John 15:19). History proves both edges: Cain and Abel head "two classes that will exist in the world till the close of time," divided over the appointed sacrifice (PP 72.5; COL 152.1; PP 74.2), and the antediluvian mingling of the Sethite and Cainite lines — "little by little" — dissolved the distinction and lost the holy character of the woman's seed (PP 81.2; SR 62.1). The standing danger this study traces is the losing of the enmity; the standing hope is that the war God declared at Eden He finishes — the dragon, "that old serpent" (Rev. 12:9), spends his last wrath on a remnant that still keeps the commandments of God and the testimony of Jesus (Rev. 12:17; MWV2 213.1). Two seeds, one war, no neutral ground: everything that follows in this handbook traces this single antagonism from Eden to the remnant.

Symbols defined here:

  • the enmity = the God-put antagonism between the two seeds — grace, not curse: fallen man is naturally at peace with the serpent, so "I will put enmity" is a supernatural interposition of implanted grace, creating "conflict where hitherto had been peace"; to lose it by befriending the world is to become "the enemy of God," and the world's hatred of the saints is the same enmity running outward (Gen. 3:15; Jas. 4:4; John 15:19; GC 505.2; GC 506.2).
  • the seed of the woman = Christ first, and in Him His people — the singular seed "which is Christ," reckoned to all who are Christ's, sown by the Son of man as the children of the kingdom, sharing the head-bruising victory, and terminating in "the remnant of her seed" who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus (Gen. 3:15; Gal. 3:16; Gal. 3:29; Matt. 13:37-38; Rom. 16:20; Rev. 12:17).
  • the seed of the serpent = a spiritual paternity, not a bloodline — those who belong to the devil by doing his works: "of your father the devil" by doing his lusts, "the children of the wicked one" sown as tares, Cain "of that wicked one" though Eve's own son; the test is practice — "he that committeth sin is of the devil," "whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God" (John 8:44; Matt. 13:38-39; 1 John 3:12; 1 John 3:8; 1 John 3:10).

Symbols carried: none — this is the opening section, establishing the charter (Gen. 3:15) on which the whole handbook stands: the two seeds, the paternity-by-practice that defines them, and the God-put enmity whose keeping or losing the following sections trace from Cain's altar to the dragon's war on the remnant.

For discussion:

  1. "This enmity is not naturally entertained" (GC 505.2) — fallen man is at peace with Satan until grace "creates conflict where hitherto had been peace" (GC 506.2; Gen. 3:15). If felt conflict with sin is the evidence of implanted grace, what does a comfortable, conflict-free spiritual life actually indicate — and how should that change the way we pray about our own complacency?
  2. Cain shared Abel's parents, yet was "of that wicked one" (1 John 3:12); the men of John 8 claimed Abraham, yet were "of your father the devil" because "the lusts of your father ye will do" (John 8:44). If seed-membership is by practice and paternity, not pedigree or profession, by what test does John say the two classes "are manifest" (1 John 3:10) — and where does that test land on us?
  3. The Sethites kept their "peculiar, holy character" while separate, and lost it "little by little" by mingling (PP 81.2; SR 62.1) — while at the end the dragon still finds "the remnant of her seed" keeping the commandments of God (Rev. 12:17). What "little by little" minglings today most quietly dissolve the God-put enmity in a family or a church, and what would it cost this week to keep the line distinct?

¶2. Cain and Abel — the Two Worships

The two classes first appear at an altar: two brothers, two offerings, two worships — the appointed lamb brought by faith, and the fruit of man's own way — and the enmity announced in Eden draws its first blood over worship.

The enmity comes to the altar — two brothers, two callings — Gen. 3:15; 4:2:

  • Gen. 3:15. "I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed" — the charter carried in from Eden (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall"): the God-put enmity between the two seeds first draws blood at Cain's altar; the worship war is the seed war.
  • Gen. 4:2. "And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground." — the two brothers, two callings: the shepherd who will bring a lamb and the tiller who will bring the ground's fruit. The two worships are seeded before the altar is built.

The two offerings — the appointed lamb and the fruit of the ground — Gen. 4:3-5; John 1:29; Heb. 11:4; Col. 2:23:

  • Gen. 4:3. "And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD." — Cain's offering: the fruit of the ground — his own labor, his own way, bloodless. The Bible's first false worship, worship on man's terms.
    • Cain's offering (the fruit of the ground) = will-worship: the self-chosen, bloodless way substituted for God's appointed way, and refused of God (Gen. 4:3; Gen. 4:5; Gen. 4:7; Col. 2:23). Defined in full at the close.
  • Gen. 4:4. "And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering" — Abel's offering: the firstlings of the flock — the appointed lamb, brought by faith, pointing to the Lamb of God. God has respect to it; the appointed way is accepted.
    • Abel's offering (the firstlings of his flock) = the appointed lamb brought by faith — righteousness by faith enacted at the world's first altar (Gen. 4:4; Heb. 11:4; John 1:29; Gen. 3:15). Defined in full at the close.
  • John 1:29. "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world." — defines what Abel's firstling meant: the appointed lamb was the shadow of THE Lamb of God. To bring the lamb by faith was to confess the coming Redeemer; to withhold it was to reject Him.
  • Heb. 11:4. "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts" — heaven's verdict on the two altars: by FAITH Abel's was more excellent. The difference was faith in the appointed sacrifice, not the quality of produce — righteousness by faith at the first altar.
  • Gen. 4:5. "But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell." — the self-chosen way is refused, and the refused worshiper turns wroth. The refusal, not favoritism, brings the Eden-planted enmity of Gen. 3:15 to its first outbreak at the altar.
  • Col. 2:23. "Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship" — Scripture's name for self-devised worship — the principle of Cain's offering: WILL worship — worship devised by the human will, wearing a shew of wisdom yet refused by God. Cain's fruit-offering is the archetype.
  • PP 71.2. White: "they were to show their faith in the blood of Christ as the promised atonement by offering the firstlings of the flock in sacrifice. Besides this, the first fruits of the earth were to be presented before the Lord as a thank offering" — defines the two offerings from the appointment itself: the firstling was the God-ordained faith-offering pointing to Christ's blood; the fruit was only a thank offering, never a substitute for the lamb.
  • PP 71.3. White: "Abel presented a sacrifice from the flock, in accordance with the Lord's directions... But Cain, disregarding the Lord's direct and explicit command, presented only an offering of fruit" — the contrast fixed: obedience to God's prescribed worship versus disregard of a direct command.
  • 3SG 48.1. White: "Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock, and of the fat as God had commanded; and in full faith of the Messiah to come... A light flashes from Heaven and consumes the offering of Abel. Cain sees no manifestation that his is accepted" — the early (1864) witness: the firstling brought "as God had commanded" in faith of the coming Messiah, heavenly fire on the appointed offering and none on Cain's.
  • PP 72.1. White: "He chose the course of self-dependence. He would come in his own merits... Cain obeyed in building an altar, obeyed in bringing a sacrifice; but he rendered only a partial obedience. The essential part, the recognition of the need of a Redeemer, was left out" — names the will-worship exactly: self-dependence, his own merits, partial obedience omitting faith in the Redeemer (Col. 2:23).
  • PP 72.3. White: "Through the shed blood he looked to the future sacrifice, Christ dying on the cross of Calvary; and trusting in the atonement that was there to be made, he had the witness that he was righteous" — confirms Heb. 11:4: Abel's offering was righteousness by faith, the shed blood looking forward to Calvary.

The door stood open — the rejection was of the way, not the man — Gen. 4:7; Prov. 14:12; John 4:23:

  • Gen. 4:7. "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door." — God's own testimony that Cain was not the victim of arbitrary rejection: the door to acceptance stood open; the issue was doing well — coming God's appointed way.
  • PP 72.4. White: "Cain had the same opportunity of learning and accepting these truths as had Abel. He was not the victim of an arbitrary purpose... Abel chose faith and obedience; Cain, unbelief and rebellion. Here the whole matter rested" — guards Gen. 4:7: the rejection was of Cain's chosen way, not an arbitrary decree; two worships, two free choices.
  • Prov. 14:12. "There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death." — the way of Cain in a proverb: a self-chosen worship that seems right to the man ends in death — first Abel's, then, in the war it opens, the worshiper's own.
  • John 4:23. "the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him." — the permanent test surfaced at Cain's altar: God seeks worship in spirit and in TRUTH — His appointed way — not worship on the worshiper's own invented terms.
  • PP 73.1. White: "The class of worshipers who follow the example of Cain includes by far the greater portion of the world; for nearly every false religion has been based on the same principle—that man can depend upon his own efforts for salvation" — the fountainhead named: Cain's altar heads the world's false worship, self-effort without the blood.

False worship persecutes true — the first martyr dies over worship — Gen. 4:8; 1 John 3:12; Matt. 23:35:

  • Gen. 4:8. "Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him." — false worship persecutes true worship: the first murder is a worship murder, the rejected worshiper killing the accepted one. The first martyr dies over worship.
  • 1 John 3:12. "Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous." — the motive named: Cain was OF that wicked one — the serpent's seed by spiritual paternity (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall") — and he slew because the righteous worship condemned his own.
  • Matt. 23:35. "from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar." — Christ names "righteous Abel" the first of the martyrs' line: the persecuting stream of false worship runs unbroken from Abel's blood to blood shed at the temple altar itself.
  • PP 74.2. White: "Cain hated and killed his brother, not for any wrong that Abel had done... So in all ages the wicked have hated those who were better than themselves. Abel's life of obedience and unswerving faith was to Cain a perpetual reproof" — the persecution principle of all ages: the righteous life reproves the false worshiper, and the false worshiper answers with the sword.

Out from the presence — the way of Cain becomes a lineage — Gen. 4:16; Jude 1:11:

  • Gen. 4:16. "And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden." — the self-appointed worshiper departs from God's presence and founds a rival line; the going-out that follows refused worship.
  • Jude 1:11. "Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain" — "the way of Cain" becomes a named, transmissible apostasy, set beside Balaam's hire and Korah's rebellion against appointed worship. A woe rests on all who walk it.
    • the way of Cain = self-appointed worship that hardens into a lineage and ends in persecuting the true (Jude 1:11; 1 John 3:12; Gen. 4:8; Matt. 23:35). Defined in full at the close.
  • PP 81.1. White: "He had gone out from the presence of the Lord... thus standing at the head of that great class of men who worship the god of this world" — Gen. 4:16 as the founding of a rival worship-line: Cain heads "that great class of men who worship the god of this world."
  • COL 200.2. White: "As Cain went out from the presence of the Lord to seek his home; as the prodigal wandered into the 'far country,' so do sinners seek happiness in forgetfulness of God" — Cain's going-out is the standing type of the sinner's self-chosen separation from God's presence.
  • PP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate... The children of Seth went 'in the way of Cain' (Jude 11); they fixed their minds upon worldly prosperity and enjoyment and neglected the commandments of the Lord" — names "the two classes" outright and shows the way of Cain is transmissible even to the covenant line: true worship kept pure by distinction, corrupted by mingling (traced in "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity").

DEFINITION — CAIN AND ABEL — THE TWO WORSHIPS = the two seeds of Gen. 3:15 first stand visible at an altar, as two worships. One generation from Eden, the shepherd and the tiller bring their offerings (Gen. 4:2-4): Abel the firstlings of the flock — the appointed lamb, brought by faith, confessing the coming Lamb of God (Heb. 11:4; John 1:29) — and Cain the fruit of the ground, his own labor offered his own way, the Bible's first false worship (Gen. 4:3). God has respect to the appointed way and not to the self-chosen one (Gen. 4:4-5), yet the rejection is of the way, not the man: "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?" (Gen. 4:7; PP 72.4). Scripture names Cain's principle "will worship" — a shew of wisdom, refused by God (Col. 2:23) — the way that "seemeth right unto a man" but ends in death (Prov. 14:12), the standing opposite of worship "in spirit and in truth" (John 4:23); and Ellen White names its posterity: "the class of worshipers who follow the example of Cain includes by far the greater portion of the world" (PP 73.1). Refused worship turns persecutor: Cain, "of that wicked one," slays his brother "because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous" (1 John 3:12; Gen. 4:8) — the serpent-seed's signature attack on God's appointed worship, and the opening of the martyr stream Christ dates "from the blood of righteous Abel" (Matt. 23:35). Cain then "went out from the presence of the LORD" (Gen. 4:16) to head "that great class of men who worship the god of this world" (PP 81.1), and his way becomes a named, walkable apostasy — "the way of Cain" (Jude 1:11) — self-appointed worship that persecutes the true. Here the whole controversy is cast in miniature: two seeds, two altars, two worships — the appointed way accepted, the self-chosen way refused, and the refused slaying the accepted — the pattern that runs in blood from Abel's field and terminates at the end of the age in the final contest over worship, the seal or the mark (see "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible"). The two worships become two civilizations in "The Two Lineages — the City and the Name."

Symbols defined here:

  • Abel's offering (the firstlings of his flock) = the appointed lamb brought by faith — righteousness by faith enacted at the world's first altar, the firstling's blood confessing the coming Lamb of God who takes away sin; accepted because it comes God's appointed way, trusting wholly in the promised atonement (Gen. 4:4; Heb. 11:4; John 1:29; Gen. 3:15).
  • Cain's offering (the fruit of the ground) = will-worship: the self-chosen, bloodless way substituted for God's appointed way — the first false worship; partial obedience (an altar, a gift) that omits the essential thing, faith in the promised Redeemer's blood, and comes in the worshiper's own merits, and to which God has not respect (Gen. 4:3; Gen. 4:5; Gen. 4:7; Col. 2:23).
  • the way of Cain = self-appointed worship that hardens into a lineage and ends in persecuting the true — the false worshiper hating and slaying the true because his own works are evil and his brother's righteous; the pattern that opens the martyr stream from righteous Abel onward (Jude 1:11; 1 John 3:12; Gen. 4:8; Matt. 23:35).

Symbols carried: the seed of the woman, the seed of the serpent, and the enmity — the God-put antagonism here drawing its first blood, Cain being "of that wicked one" (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall"); Cain's going out from the presence of the LORD, which becomes the first city and the rival civilization (see "The Two Lineages — the City and the Name"); the corruption of the covenant line that later walks "in the way of Cain" (see "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity"); and the worship war's terminus, where the two worships stand fully formed as they that worship the beast and they that keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus (see "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible").

For discussion:

  1. Cain "obeyed in building an altar, obeyed in bringing a sacrifice; but he rendered only a partial obedience" (PP 72.1), and God told him the door stood open: "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?" (Gen. 4:7). Where in our own worship do we bring the altar and the gift but withhold "the essential part, the recognition of the need of a Redeemer" — and how would we know?
  2. "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain" (Heb. 11:4) — the difference was not the produce but faith in the appointed Lamb (John 1:29). What does it mean that righteousness by faith is enacted at the very first altar in Scripture, and how does that guard us from thinking acceptance with God was ever, in any age, by man's own efforts (PP 73.1)?
  3. Cain slew Abel "because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous" (1 John 3:12), and "Abel's life of obedience and unswerving faith was to Cain a perpetual reproof" (PP 74.2). If false worship still answers the reproof of the righteous with hostility, what should the accepted worshiper expect (Matt. 23:35) — and how does Abel's altar, not Cain's sword, remain his only weapon?

¶3. The Two Lineages — the City and the Name

The two worships become two civilizations: Cain's line goes out from the Presence and builds a city; Seth's line stays and calls upon the name of the LORD — and from Genesis 4 to Revelation the war of the two classes runs on between the city and the Name.

From the altar to the city — the worship-war becomes a civilization — Gen. 4:3, 5, 16-17:

  • Gen. 4:3. "Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD" — the self-appointed offering: worship on man's own terms, the fruit of the cursed ground and his own labor, refusing the blood (the first false worship, defined in "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships"). The city-line's religion begins at this altar.
  • Gen. 4:5. "But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell" — God's non-respect for the self-willed offering ignites the wrath that becomes murder (v. 8) and then a civilization (v. 17). The two lineages divide first at the altar, then spread into two peoples.
  • COL 152.1. White: "The Pharisee and the publican represent two great classes... Their first two representatives are found in the first two children that were born into the world" — the perennial two classes of worshipers are rooted in the two offerings; what Genesis 4 now traces is those two worships hardening into two lineages.
  • Gen. 4:16. "And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden" — the city-line begins with a departure. Everything Cain builds afterward is built by a fugitive from the face of God; he settles away from the Presence, and the geography of the two classes is born here.
  • Gen. 4:17. "he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch" — the first city in Scripture: built by the first murderer, self-named and self-perpetuating. Cain, cut off from the Name, makes a name.
    • the city of Cain = the serpent-seed's congregation — fortified convenience built by the fugitive from God's presence: man staying put in the cursed earth, distinguished in arts, industry, and violence-as-culture while God is forgotten; the civilization whose spirit prevails in the eating-drinking-marrying world Christ names as the type of the last age (Gen. 4:16-17; Gen. 4:21-23; Matt. 24:38; PP 81.1).
  • PP 81.1. White: "He had gone out from the presence of the Lord, cast away the promise of the restored Eden, to seek his possessions and enjoyment in the earth under the curse of sin, thus standing at the head of that great class of men who worship the god of this world" — Cain heads a CLASS, not merely a family: the worshipers of the god of this world, seeking their portion in the earth under the curse.

The city's culture — the home broken, the arts advancing, violence sung — Gen. 4:19-24; Gen. 2:24; Matt. 19:4-8:

  • Gen. 4:19. "And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah" — the first polygamist, fifth in Cain's line. The serpent-seed's assault on the FIRST institution of Eden — marriage — is now culture, not lapse.
  • Gen. 2:24. "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" — the Eden charter Lamech breaks: one man, one wife, one flesh. The war of the two lineages runs through the home, not merely the altar.
  • Matt. 19:4. "he which made them at the beginning made them male and female" — Christ roots marriage in creation; the Cainite innovation is a departure from the order the Maker fixed.
  • Matt. 19:6. "What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder" — Lamech's two wives put asunder what God joined: the city-line remaking the home to suit itself.
  • Matt. 19:8. "from the beginning it was not so" — Christ's rule against every corruption of marriage back to Eden; the Cainite polygamy is judged by the original, unbroken pattern.
  • Gen. 4:21. "he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ" — Jubal: music and culture flourish inside the city of Cain — refinement without repentance, arts advancing while God is forgotten.
  • Gen. 4:22. "Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron" — metallurgy and industry, the technological genius of the Cainite city. The line godless in worship is distinguished in earthly and material progress.
  • PP 81.1. White: "In that which pertains to mere earthly and material progress, his descendants became distinguished... To the crime of murder, in which Cain had led the way, Lamech, the fifth in descent, added polygamy" — the two marks of the city named together: material brilliance, and the broken home.
  • Gen. 4:23. "for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt" — Lamech's sword-song: violence set to poetry, boasted openly to his two wives. Cain's murder has become the city's culture; bloodshed is now sung, not hidden.
  • Gen. 4:24. "If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold" — God's protective word over Cain twisted into a boast of self-vengeance. The city-line's religion is self-serving even where it names God.

The Name — the faithful seed re-established — Gen. 4:25-26; Luke 3:38:

  • Gen. 4:25. "For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew" — the faithful seed re-established in Seth: "another seed" in the room of the martyr. The two lineages are now formally set — the line of the murderer and the line of the appointed seed.
  • Luke 3:38. "Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God" — the genealogy of Christ runs through Enos and Seth to "the son of God": the Sethite stream is the covenant line, the lineage of the promised Seed of "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall."
  • Gen. 4:26. "then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" — the dividing act of the faithful seed. Cain named a city after his son; Seth's line calls on the Name of the LORD. Not a wall but a confessed allegiance marks off the faithful.
    • calling on the name of the LORD = the dividing act of the faithful seed — open, avowed worship: a public profession of loyalty to God that marks off the Sethite line from the city; its living crown is Enoch, who walked with God in the corrupt age and preached judgment to the very city of Cain (Gen. 4:26; Gen. 5:24; Jude 1:14-15).
  • PP 80.2. White: "The faithful had worshiped God before; but as men increased, the distinction between the two classes became more marked. There was an open profession of loyalty to God on the part of one, as there was of contempt and disobedience on the part of the other" — the definition confirmed: what began at Enos was not worship itself but MARKED worship, the open profession that makes the two classes visible.

The crown of the calling line — Enoch, the seventh from Adam — Gen. 5:22, 24; Jude 1:14-15:

  • Gen. 5:22. "And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters" — the walk was not a hermit's trance but the whole tenor of a working life: husband, father, citizen, three hundred years of communion in the heart of a corrupt age.
  • PP 85.1. White: "Enoch's walk with God was not in a trance or vision, but in all the duties of his daily life... as a husband and father, a friend, a citizen, he was the steadfast, unwavering servant of the Lord" — calling on the Name embodied: open, avowed faithfulness lived out in the ordinary offices of life.
  • GW 52.1. White: "In the midst of a life of active labor, Enoch steadfastly maintained his communion with God... he would withdraw, to spend a season in solitude" — Enoch's rhythm of withdrawal and return is the personal form of the Sethite separation: apart to commune, back to labor.
  • GW 51.2. White: "The infinite, unfathomable love of God through Christ, became the subject of his meditations day and night. With all the fervor of his soul he sought to reveal that love to the people among whom he dwelt" — the inner spring of the walk: communion kept apart, then poured out toward the people — separation that exists for testimony, not escape.
  • Gen. 5:24. "And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him" — the crown of the Sethite stream: the man who held the upward current while the world flowed the other way is translated. Proof that the calling-on-the-Name line can be kept pure in the midst of the city's age.
  • Jude 1:14. "And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints" — the New Testament fixes Enoch as the seventh from Adam and the first advent preacher: the faithful line's witness is judgment-preaching from the beginning.
  • MWV2 17.3. Miller: "Jude tells us that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, Behold the Lord cometh, with ten thousands of his saints" — the pioneer of the advent movement stands Enoch at the head of his own line of evidence: the second-advent hope is as old as the seventh from Adam.
  • Jude 1:15. "To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them" — Enoch's message was a warning of judgment on the ungodly city-line: the faithful seed does not merely withdraw; it testifies against the civilization it separates from.
  • PP 86.1. White: "His labors were not restricted to the Sethites. In the land where Cain had sought to flee from the divine Presence, the prophet of God made known the wonderful scenes that had passed before his vision" — separation is not silence: the mountain-line carried the warning down into the very land of Cain's flight.

Mountains and plains — the geography of the two classes — Gen. 4:16; 6:1-2:

  • mountains and plains = the geography of the two classes: the Cainites, spreading from their first settlement away from the Presence, dispersed over the plains and valleys; the Sethites, to escape their contaminating influence, withdrew to the mountains — God's people dwelling apart, the serpent's seed congregating for convenience. This is the geography of SEPARATION, not of appointed worship — worship is "in spirit and in truth" wherever the faithful are (John 4:21-24); the mountain is where the peculiar character is kept, not where God is uniquely found. Scripture gives the pattern its own voice in the angel's word to Lot, "Escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed" (Gen. 19:17; taken up in "Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain") (Gen. 4:16; Gen. 6:1; Gen. 6:2; Gen. 19:17).
  • PP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate. The race of Cain... dispersed over the plains and valleys where the children of Seth had dwelt; and the latter, in order to escape from their contaminating influence, withdrew to the mountains, and there made their home. So long as this separation continued, they maintained the worship of God in its purity" — THE ANCHOR: "the two classes" named outright, the mountain/plain geography given exactly, and the doctrinal weight stated — separation preserved pure worship.
  • Gen. 6:1. "when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them" — the setting for the fatal breakdown of the separation the mountains had kept.
  • Gen. 6:2. "the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" — the sons of God = the covenant line of Seth (Luke 3:38), not angels; the descent from the mountains to marry the city dissolves the peculiar character of the faithful (walked in full in "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity").
  • Gen. 6:5. "every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" — the moral fruit of the merged lineages: when the two classes mingle, the Cainite spirit prevails, and the whole earth is condemned.
  • GC 65.3. White: "Behind the lofty bulwarks of the mountains—in all ages the refuge of the persecuted and oppressed—the Waldenses found a hiding place. Here the light of truth was kept burning amid the darkness of the Middle Ages" — the geography recurs through history: the mountains keep the faith while the plains keep the world (traced in "The Church in the Wilderness — the Mountains Keep the Faith").

The end-time antitype — the city civilization named for the last days — Matt. 24:38:

  • Matt. 24:38. "For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark" — Christ names the world the Cainite city-spirit conquered as the type of the last age. Note what damns it: not open atheism but appetite and self-indulgent normalcy — eating, drinking, marrying — the city of Cain's spirit running at full culture until the door shuts.
  • DA 633.1. White: "Christ does not here bring to view a temporal millennium... He tells us that as it was in Noah's day, so will it be when the Son of man comes again" — the two-lineages pattern is prophetically appointed, not merely historical: the last generation replays the city and the Name.
  • TTAM 6.1. J. White: "In the third angel's message... but two classes are brought to view. One is oppressive, and persecutes the saints, and has the mark of the beast... The other class is oppressed and driven... and are sealed with the seal of the living God by keeping 'the commandments of God'" — the pioneer witness confirms independently that at the end only two classes exist: the marked and the sealed. That this final division is the antitype of Genesis 4's two lineages is this handbook's argument, drawn out in "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible."

DEFINITION — THE TWO LINEAGES — THE CITY AND THE NAME = the two worships of the first altar (Gen. 4:3-5) harden into two civilizations. Cain, having "gone out from the presence of the LORD" (Gen. 4:16), "builded a city" (Gen. 4:17) — the first in Scripture, built by a fugitive and named for his son — and his line fills it with the marks of the class: the home broken by Lamech's polygamy against the one-flesh charter of Eden (Gen. 4:19; Gen. 2:24; Matt. 19:4-8), the arts and industry of Jubal and Tubalcain advancing while God is forgotten (Gen. 4:21-22; PP 81.1), and violence sung as culture in Lamech's sword-song (Gen. 4:23-24). Over against the city stands the Name: the faithful seed re-established in Seth, "another seed instead of Abel" (Gen. 4:25), the covenant line of the genealogy of Christ (Luke 3:38), marked off not by a wall but by open, avowed worship — "then began men to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen. 4:26; PP 80.2) — and crowned in Enoch, the seventh from Adam, who "walked with God" through all the duties of a working life (Gen. 5:22, 24; PP 85.1) and carried the first advent-and-judgment sermon into the very land of Cain's flight (Jude 1:14-15; PP 86.1; MWV2 17.3). The two classes take a geography: Cainites over the plains and valleys, Sethites withdrawn to the mountains, and "so long as this separation continued, they maintained the worship of God in its purity" (PP 81.2) — until the sons of God came down to marry the daughters of men and the merged earth grew "only evil continually" (Gen. 6:1-2, 5). Christ appoints this whole picture to the last days: "as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage" (Matt. 24:38; DA 633.1), and the pioneer witness confirms that at the end "but two classes are brought to view," the marked and the sealed (TTAM 6.1). Every soul stands in the city or calls on the Name; there is no third lineage.

Symbols defined here:

  • the city of Cain = the serpent-seed's congregation — fortified convenience built by the fugitive from God's presence; man staying put in the cursed earth, distinguished in arts, industry, and violence-as-culture while God is forgotten; the civilization whose spirit prevails in the eating-drinking-marrying world Christ names as the type of the last age (Gen. 4:16-17; Gen. 4:21-23; Matt. 24:38; PP 81.1).
  • calling on the name of the LORD = the dividing act of the faithful seed — open, avowed worship, a public profession of loyalty that marks off the Sethite line from the city; crowned in Enoch, who walked with God in the corrupt age and preached judgment to the city of Cain (Gen. 4:26; Gen. 5:24; Jude 1:14-15; PP 80.2).
  • mountains and plains = the geography of the two classes — the serpent's seed congregating over the plains and valleys for convenience, the faithful withdrawing to the mountains to keep their peculiar character and their worship pure; the geography of separation, not of appointed worship, given its biblical voice in "Escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed" (Gen. 4:16; Gen. 6:1-2; Gen. 19:17; PP 81.2; GC 65.3).

Symbols carried: the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent, and the God-put enmity these lineages embody (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall"); Cain's offering and the way of Cain, the two worships from which the two civilizations grow (see "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships"); the mingling of Gen. 6:1-5, only opened here, walked in full where it belongs (see "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity"); the city, carried forward to its congregating charter and its prophetic climax (see "Babel — Congregating for Convenience"; "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call"); the mountain refuge recurring through history (see "The Church in the Wilderness — the Mountains Keep the Faith"); the days-of-Noah antitype and the final two companies (see "As in the Days of Noah — the Last Mingling"; "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible").

For discussion:

  1. The two lineages divide first at the altar — Cain's offering of his own labor against the blood (Gen. 4:3-5) — and only afterward become two civilizations. Where in your own worship do you bring God "the fruit of the ground," terms of your own appointing, rather than what He has appointed — and why does self-willed worship, not open atheism, head the city-line?
  2. Cain, cut off from the Presence, "builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son" (Gen. 4:17) — he lost the Name and made a name — while Seth's line "began... to call upon the name of the LORD" (Gen. 4:26) as "an open profession of loyalty" (PP 80.2). Where in your own life are you building a name — security, reputation, accumulation — in place of openly calling on the Name?
  3. The city of Cain was brilliant: harp and organ, brass and iron (Gen. 4:21-22) — "distinguished" in "mere earthly and material progress" (PP 81.1) — and Christ says the last days will look exactly like it: "eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage" (Matt. 24:38). If what damned the city-line was not open atheism but self-indulgent normalcy, how do we tell whether our own work, art, and comfort are Sethite labor or Cainite culture?

Part II — The Mingling and the Flood

¶4. The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity

The peculiar people were not destroyed by persecution but dissolved by alliance: the sons of God saw, chose by sight, and took wives of the daughters of men — and when the two classes became one flesh, the distinction God had put between them was gone, "all flesh had corrupted his way," and the faithful stream shrank to eight souls. The mingling is the standing mechanism of apostasy: the world never rises to the church; the church always descends to the world.

The two lines before the union — pilgrims and the world-worshiping class — Gen. 2:24; 4:19; Deut. 14:1-2:

  • Gen. 2:24. "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" — Eden's marriage institution: one man, one wife, one flesh. This is the standard against which the ruin of this section is measured; the attack falls not on a human custom but on a gift from before sin.
  • Gen. 4:19. "And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah" — polygamy begins in Cain's line, the fifth from the fugitive who "went out from the presence of the LORD" (Gen. 4:16; see "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships"). Before the mingling, the corruption of marriage is confined to the serpent's seed; the mingling is how it crosses the line.
  • Deut. 14:1-2. "Ye are the children of the LORD your God... For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God, and the LORD hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth" — Scripture's own idiom: "children of the LORD" names the professed covenant people, and their calling is PECULIARITY — set apart above the nations. This is the very thing the mingling dissolves.
  • PP 81.1. White: "thus standing at the head of that great class of men who worship the god of this world.... To the crime of murder, in which Cain had led the way, Lamech, the fifth in descent, added polygamy.... the descendants of Seth... counting themselves 'strangers and pilgrims on the earth'" — the two lines drawn before the union: Cain's, the world-worshiping class with polygamy already in it; Seth's, the pilgrim people.
  • GSAM 40.1. Loughborough: "Afterward Seth was counted in the line of descent from Adam.... Cain, the real first-born, is not counted in the pedigree.... after the birth of Seth, men began to call themselves by the name of the Lord" — the pioneer witness to the historical fact of two genealogical streams: Seth counted in the covenant pedigree, Cain excluded, the Sethites bearing the Lord's name (see "The Two Lineages — the City and the Name").

Scripture defines its own phrase — who are the sons of God? — Gen. 6:1-2; Luke 3:38; Matt. 22:30:

  • Gen. 6:1-2. "And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" — the text of the ruin. Two classes, one act: the sons of God SAW, judged by the sight of the eyes ("fair"), and TOOK "wives of all which they chose" — choice unbounded by God's counsel, and in "all which they chose" the plural liberty of Lamech now practiced in the faithful line.
    • the sons of God = the covenant line of Seth, the professed people of God. Scripture defines the phrase in this very genealogy: Adam is "the son of God" (Luke 3:38), and the covenant people are "the children of the LORD your God," a "peculiar people" (Deut. 14:1-2) — read literally, per Miller's Rule, not angels, "for in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven" (Matt. 22:30) (Gen. 6:2; Luke 3:38; Deut. 14:1; Matt. 22:30).
    • the daughters of men = the Cainite line, the world — the daughters of the "men" who "began to multiply on the face of the earth" (Gen. 6:1), the class descended from the man who "went out from the presence of the LORD" (Gen. 4:16), into which polygamy had already entered (Gen. 4:19) (Gen. 6:1-2; Gen. 4:16; Gen. 4:19).
  • Luke 3:38. "Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God" — Scripture's own definition, planted in the antediluvian genealogy itself: "son of God" is covenant language for Adam and his faithful line. The Bible defines its own figures; no angel-mythology is needed or allowed.
  • Matt. 22:30. "For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven" — Christ's own testimony closes the door on the angel reading of Gen. 6:2: angels do not marry. The widespread "sons of God = angels" interpretation is excluded on Scripture's own terms — the sons of God are men of the covenant line, and the tragedy of Genesis 6 is a CHURCH tragedy, not a monster story.
  • CTr 39.2. White: "The worshipers of God called themselves the sons of God," and "there were two parties in the world then, and there always will be" — the most direct inspired confirmation of the Sethite reading: the phrase of Gen. 6:2 is the self-designation of the worshipers of God, and the two-party division it records is universalized — "there always will be." The Genesis 6 division is the division of this whole study (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall").

The mechanism of ruin — saw, chose, took — Gen. 6:2; PP 81.2; AH 121.3:

  • Gen. 6:2. "the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" — mark the verbs: SAW (attraction), CHOSE (alliance), TOOK (descent). Not one word of persecution, compulsion, or heresy — the peculiar people were not conquered; they married.
    • the mingling = the alliance of the two classes by which the peculiar people lose their peculiarity — the standing mechanism of apostasy. The sons of God chose by sight and took "wives of all which they chose" (Gen. 6:2), and the end was that "all flesh had corrupted his way" (Gen. 6:12); the abiding law is one-directional — the yoke of light with darkness is forbidden (2 Cor. 6:14), "evil communications corrupt good manners" (1 Cor. 15:33), "the friendship of the world is enmity with God" (Jas. 4:4) — the church descends, the world never rises (Gen. 6:1-5; Gen. 6:12; 2 Cor. 6:14; 1 Cor. 15:33; Jas. 4:4).
  • PP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate.... the latter, in order to escape from their contaminating influence, withdrew to the mountains, and there made their home.... But in the lapse of time they ventured, little by little, to mingle with the inhabitants of the valleys.... The children of Seth, attracted by the beauty of the daughters of Cain's descendants, displeased the Lord by intermarrying with them.... they lost their peculiar, holy character" — the load-bearing anchor, and the section's title in her own words: the separation held, the descent came "little by little," the attraction was by beauty, the act was intermarriage, and the loss was exactly "their peculiar, holy character." The same paragraph converts two inferences into cited fact: "the restrictions of the seventh commandment were disregarded, 'and they took them wives of all which they chose'" — Lamech's plural liberty (Gen. 4:19) now practiced in the faithful line — and the mingled Sethites went "in the way of Cain" (Jude 11; see "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships").
  • CTr 39.2. White: "The descendants of Seth went up into the mountains and there made themselves homes separate from the sons of Cain.... But after the exhortations and the influence of Enoch were removed from them, they commenced to unite with the descendants of Cain" — the timing: the separation held only while Enoch's voice held; when the living witness was removed, the union began. Distinction is not self-sustaining; it must be kept.
  • AH 121.3. White: "There is in itself no sin in eating and drinking, or in marrying and giving in marriage. It was lawful to marry in the time of Noah, and it is lawful to marry now.... But in the days of Noah men married without consulting God or seeking His guidance and counsel" — the sin located precisely: not marriage, which is Eden's own institution (Gen. 2:24), but marriage by the sight of the eyes without God — "wives of all which they chose." The lawful thing, taken out of God's hand, became the instrument of ruin.

The result — the distinction dissolves, corruption is total — Gen. 6:5, 11-12; 1 Cor. 15:33:

  • Gen. 6:5. "And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" — the sons of God "saw" and took; now GOD saw. Once the distinction dissolved, corruption ran without remainder — "every imagination... only evil continually" — thought itself apostate.
  • Gen. 6:11-12. "The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence. And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth" — "ALL flesh": the two classes have become one class. The union did not lift the Cainites; it erased the Sethites.
  • 1 Cor. 15:33. "Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners" — the apostle states the one-directional law the antediluvian record demonstrates: corrupt association corrupts good character, never the reverse. "Be not deceived" — the deception is precisely the hope that the mingling will run uphill.
  • AH 460.1. White: "It was by associating with idolaters and joining in their festivities that the Hebrews were led to transgress God's law.... So now it is by leading the followers of Christ to associate with the ungodly and unite in their amusements that Satan is most successful in alluring them into sin.... God requires of His people now as great a distinction from the world, in customs, habits, and principles, as He required of Israel anciently" — the law confirmed across every age: association allures the faithful downward, and the required distinction is undiminished now.

The remnant of the unmingled — Gen. 6:8-9; 1 Pet. 3:20:

  • Gen. 6:8-9. "But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.... Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God" — against "all flesh," one "but." Noah is "perfect in his generations" — his family line unmingled, the distinction kept — and he "walked with God" as Enoch had. When the class dissolved, the enmity survived in one house.
  • 1 Pet. 3:20. "when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water" — the arithmetic of the mingling: the covenant line, once a class filling the mountains, is "few, that is, eight souls." When the church marries the world, it is the church that is lost — the world remains, eight souls come out of it.

The lesson codified into law — no yoke with darkness — Deut. 7:3-4; 2 Cor. 6:14-17; Jas. 4:4:

  • Deut. 7:3-4. "Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son. For they will turn away thy son from following me... and destroy thee suddenly" — God writes the antediluvian lesson into covenant statute, and gives the reason: "for they will turn away thy son." The reason IS the mechanism of Genesis 6 — Infinite Wisdom legislating against the mingling because its direction never varies (the statute Israel broke; see "Israel Mingles — 'Like All the Nations'").
  • 2 Cor. 6:14. "Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?" — the New Testament form of the same law. The five questions of vv. 14-16 all expect the answer NONE: no fellowship, no communion, no concord, no part, no agreement — the two classes admit no yoke.
  • 2 Cor. 6:16-17. "ye are the temple of the living God... Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you" — the remedy for the mingling is separation, and God's reception is conditioned on it. The "come out" that closes this study is already sounding here (see "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call").
  • Jas. 4:4. "Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God" — the Genesis 6 sin transposed to the church and named ADULTERY: friendship with the world is the marriage of the sons of God to the daughters of men in its spiritual form. There is no third class — to befriend the world is to change seeds.
  • CCh 120.3. White: "The Lord commanded ancient Israel not to intermarry with the idolatrous nations around them: 'Neither shalt thou make marriages with them.'... Infinite Wisdom, foreseeing the result of such unions, declares: 'For they will turn away thy son from following Me.'... In the New Testament are similar prohibitions concerning the marriage of Christians with the ungodly" — Deuteronomy 7, the peculiar-people calling, and the unequal-yoke command bound into one continuous law flowing out of the antediluvian ruin.
  • 8MR 108.1. White: "All combinations with unbelievers that bind as a yoke must be broken. These words apply not only to making a marriage covenant with an unbeliever, but to the making of all unions where the worldly element can have a prevailing influence over believers" — the principle widened beyond marriage: EVERY alliance in which the worldly element can prevail is the Genesis 6 mechanism in another dress.
  • Ev 617.4. White: "The Lord's injunction, 'Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers,' refers not only to the marriage of Christians with the ungodly, but to all alliances in which the parties are brought into intimate association, and in which there is need of harmony in spirit and action" — the same confirmation: wherever the two classes are brought into intimate association, the unequal-yoke command stands guard.

The type stamped on the last days — Matt. 24:37-39:

  • Matt. 24:37-39. "But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away" — Christ Himself seals this section as prophecy: "marrying and giving in marriage" — the very engine of the antediluvian apostasy — is named as the sign-condition of the generation that meets Him. The mingling is not ancient history; it is the last-day mechanism, walked in full at "As in the Days of Noah — the Last Mingling."

DEFINITION — THE MINGLING — HOW THE PECULIAR PEOPLE LOST THEIR PECULIARITY = the alliance of the two classes by which the covenant people ceased to be a distinct people, and the standing mechanism of apostasy in every age. The two lines stood defined — Cain's, the world-worshiping class with polygamy already in it (Gen. 4:19; PP 81.1), Seth's, the "children of the LORD," a "peculiar people" (Deut. 14:1-2) counted in the covenant pedigree (GSAM 40.1) — until "the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" (Gen. 6:2). The sons of God are the Sethite covenant line, defined by Scripture's own genealogy — Adam "the son of God" (Luke 3:38) — confirmed by the testimony ("the worshipers of God called themselves the sons of God," CTr 39.2), and not angels, "for in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage" (Matt. 22:30). The mechanism of ruin was not persecution but marriage: attraction, alliance, descent — the lawful institution of Eden (Gen. 2:24) taken up by sight "without consulting God" (AH 121.3), "little by little" after the two classes had "for some time remained separate," until "the restrictions of the seventh commandment were disregarded" and "they lost their peculiar, holy character" (PP 81.2; CTr 39.2). The result ran one direction only: "every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually" (Gen. 6:5), "all flesh had corrupted his way" (Gen. 6:12) — the world did not rise, the church descended, for "evil communications corrupt good manners" (1 Cor. 15:33) — and the faithful stream shrank to one man "perfect in his generations" (Gen. 6:8-9) and "eight souls" (1 Pet. 3:20). God codified the lesson into law — "Neither shalt thou make marriages with them... for they will turn away thy son" (Deut. 7:3-4), "Be ye not unequally yoked... come out from among them, and be ye separate" (2 Cor. 6:14-17), extended to "all unions where the worldly element can have a prevailing influence" (8MR 108.1; Ev 617.4; CCh 120.3) — and named its church-form adultery: "the friendship of the world is enmity with God" (Jas. 4:4). And Christ stamped it on the end: "as the days of Noe were... marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark" (Matt. 24:37-39). Between the translation of Enoch and the Flood, the peculiar people unmade themselves by alliance; the same mechanism runs to the coming of the Son of man, for "there always will be" two parties (CTr 39.2). When the church marries the world, the church is what is lost.

Symbols defined here:

  • the sons of God = the covenant line of Seth, the professed people of God — Scripture's own idiom for Adam's faithful line ("the son of God," Luke 3:38) and the covenant people ("the children of the LORD your God," Deut. 14:1); read literally, not angels, for angels marry not (Gen. 6:2; Luke 3:38; Deut. 14:1-2; Matt. 22:30).
  • the daughters of men = the Cainite line, the world — the daughters of the multiplying "men" of Gen. 6:1, the class of the man who went out from the presence of the LORD, already practicing polygamy (Gen. 6:1-2; Gen. 4:16; Gen. 4:19).
  • the mingling = the alliance of the two classes by which the peculiar people lose their peculiarity — the standing mechanism of apostasy: choice by sight, union with the world, one-directional descent, ending in "all flesh had corrupted his way"; forbidden as the unequal yoke, named as the friendship of the world (Gen. 6:1-5; Gen. 6:12; 2 Cor. 6:14; 1 Cor. 15:33; Jas. 4:4).

Symbols carried: the two seeds and the enmity — the God-put antagonism this section shows being surrendered from the church's side (see "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall"); the way of Cain and the departure from the presence of the LORD (see "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships"); the two lineages, the Sethites' mountain separation, calling on the name of the LORD, and Lamech's polygamy (see "The Two Lineages — the City and the Name"); the attack on Eden's institutions that the mingling opens is traced in full at "The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack"; the last-day form of the mingling at "As in the Days of Noah — the Last Mingling"; the final visible distinction the mingling would erase at "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible"; the remedy at "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call."

For discussion:

  1. The sons of God "saw... that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" (Gen. 6:2) — and Ellen White locates the sin not in marriage but in marrying "without consulting God or seeking His guidance and counsel" (AH 121.3). Where in your own life is a LAWFUL thing being chosen by sight rather than by counsel — and what would consulting God first actually look like there?
  2. The mingling was "little by little" (PP 81.2) and its law is one-directional: "evil communications corrupt good manners" (1 Cor. 15:33) — all flesh was corrupted, and the world never rose. We often justify close alliance with the world as missionary influence. By what Scripture test can you tell whether an association is lifting them or leveling you — and what "combination that binds as a yoke" (8MR 108.1; 2 Cor. 6:14) might need to be broken?
  3. When the mingling was complete, "all flesh had corrupted his way" and the faithful were "few, that is, eight souls" (Gen. 6:12; 1 Pet. 3:20) — yet Noah stood "perfect in his generations" and "walked with God" (Gen. 6:9). Since Christ says the last generation repeats Noah's (Matt. 24:37-39), what does it take to be "perfect in his generations" — unmingled — in an age when the two classes look almost identical, and how is that separation an act of faith rather than of pride (2 Cor. 6:17)?

¶5. The Days of Noah — the Institutions of Eden Under Attack

Eden gave three gifts before sin — marriage, the appointed diet, and the Sabbath — and by Noah's day the serpent's seed had struck the first two openly and corrupted worship at its root; the flood found a world wholly absorbed in the lawful, and one household that did all God commanded.

The three gifts before sin — the institutions of Eden — Gen. 2:24; 1:29; 3:18; 2:1-3:

  • Gen. 2:24. "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh" — the FIRST institution of Eden: marriage, spoken before sin; one man, one woman, one flesh. This is the marriage law the serpent's seed will attack.
    • the institutions of Eden = the three gifts God established before sin, each rooted in Eden: MARRIAGE (Gen. 2:24, one man and one woman made one flesh), the APPOINTED DIET (Gen. 1:29, the seed-bearing herbs, fruits, and grains given for meat), and the SABBATH (Gen. 2:1-3, the seventh day blessed and sanctified). All three predate the fall; all three are assaulted by the serpent's seed running down through Cain's line — polygamy strikes marriage (Gen. 4:19; Gen. 6:2), indulged appetite strikes the diet (Matt. 24:38; Luke 17:27), and self-appointed worship strikes the appointed worship (Gen. 4:3-5; see "Cain and Abel — the Two Worships"), the last war meeting the Sabbath at the end (Rev. 13-14). Defined in full at the close.
  • Gen. 1:29. "Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat" — the SECOND gift, touching appetite: the original diet. Fruits, grains, herbs, the seed-bearing bounty; flesh is conspicuously absent from the grant.
    • the original diet = the Gen. 1:29 grant — "every herb bearing seed... and every tree... yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat" — fruits, grains, and (after the fall) the herb of the field (Gen. 3:18). Flesh was NOT granted in Eden and was not granted until after the flood (Gen. 9:3); therefore through the whole antediluvian age the vegetable grant still stood, and the days-of-Noah eating and drinking was appetite indulged against, not within, God's appointed diet. Defined in full at the close.
  • Gen. 3:18. "Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field" — after the fall the diet is enlarged to "the herb of the field" (vegetables), but still no flesh; the vegetable grant of Gen. 1:29 continues even under the curse.
  • Gen. 2:1-3. "And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day... And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it" — the THIRD institution: the Sabbath, blessed and sanctified before sin — God's own memorial of creation, the appointed rest and the appointed worship.
  • AH 340.4. White: "He referred them to the blessed days of Eden when God pronounced all things 'very good.' Then marriage and the Sabbath had their origin, twin institutions for the glory of God in the benefit of humanity" — names two of the three outright: marriage and the Sabbath, "twin institutions," born in Eden before sin, corroborating Gen. 2:24 and Gen. 2:1-3.
  • Ed 250.2. White: "The Sabbath and the family were alike instituted in Eden, and in God's purpose they are indissolubly linked together. On this day more than on any other, it is possible for us to live the life of Eden" — Sabbath and family "indissolubly linked," both Eden institutions; to keep them is to live the life of Eden.
  • CD 81.2. White: "Grains, fruits, nuts, and vegetables constitute the diet chosen for us by our Creator" — the diet confirmed: the Creator's chosen table is the Gen. 1:29 grant, flesh absent — the last of the three gifts to receive its witness.

The first blow — marriage struck in Cain's line, then in Seth's — Gen. 4:19; 6:2; Luke 3:38; Deut. 14:1:

  • Gen. 4:19. "And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah" — the serpent's seed strikes marriage first: Lamech of Cain's line is Scripture's first polygamist, breaking the one-flesh law of Gen. 2:24. The attack begins in the city-building line (see "The Two Lineages — the City and the Name").
  • Gen. 6:2. "That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose" — the attack crosses into the covenant line: marriage debased into appetite, choosing by the eye, "all which they chose." The two classes merge (the mingling itself is walked in "The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity").
  • Luke 3:38. "Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God" — Scripture's own key to Gen. 6:2: the "sons of God" are the line of Seth, traced through Enos to Adam who "was the son of God." The Bible defines its own figure — the covenant line, not angels.
